title: Talk about the problem, not yourself
header_line: My analysis of one book on authority and personal brand. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Do people hear ideas or about you?
A student described a creator with a large social following who funnels a share of the followers to paid long-form articles at a small monthly price. She does not need all of them, only a portion.
I said that by understanding your specific audience, writing about something you love, sticking to a channel and being consistent, you will grow.
I said: I do not need to talk about my company; I need to talk about an erosion problem, because then people think this is an expert. I do not have to say I am an expert.
I asked: who is likely to have more authority, people who talk about people or people who talk about ideas? I said ideas, the future, accountability, concrete language and verbs are signs of a doer.
A student said: the group runs through a lot of concepts and asked how to practice them.
I said the best way to practise is to separate two language styles.
Write one problem in your field and say three true things about it.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the problem your audience has.
Write three true things about it.
Write the verbs you will use.
Write the channel you will stick to.
Write the portion of followers you will invite deeper.

check.q: What did I say to talk about instead of your company?
What did I say signs of a doer are?
What did a student say about a funnel?
choices: You only need a portion of followers

recap: Talk about the problem. Be consistent. Use verbs.
